title: Practising for the interview
lines: Your interview is tomorrow, right? Do you want to practise?
OK. I'm the interviewer. What are your strengths?
Well... I'm hard-working and I learn fast.
Good, but give an example. Interviewers like examples.
OK. In my last job, I learned to use a new program in one week, and then I helped my colleagues.
Much better! And remember to smile and to look at the interviewer.
Thanks. What time should I leave home?
The interview is at ten, and it takes forty minutes to get there. Leave at nine, so you arrive early.

q.q: Why does the man want to practise?
q.a: Because his interview is tomorrow and he is really nervous.

q.q: What advice does the woman give about his strengths?
q.a: To give an example, because interviewers like examples.

q.q: What time should he leave home, and why?
q.a: At nine, because the interview is at ten and it takes forty minutes, so he will arrive early.

gaps.s: I learned to use a new ___ in one week.
Remember to ___ and to look at the interviewer.

title: Questions for the company
lines: That's all from my side. Do you have any questions for me?
Yes, a couple. Could you tell me what a typical day in this role looks like?
Sure. Mornings are usually spent on site with the installers, and afternoons in the office preparing documentation.
That sounds varied. And what kind of training do new employees receive?
There's a two-week induction, and after that each new engineer has a mentor for the first six months.
That's great. Finally, what are the next steps in the process?
We're interviewing two more candidates this week. We'll let everyone know by next Wednesday, and the final stage is a short technical test.
Perfect. Thank you very much for your time.

q.q: What does a typical day in the role involve?
q.a: Mornings on site with the installers and afternoons in the office preparing documentation.

q.q: What training do new employees receive?
q.a: A two-week induction and then a mentor for the first six months.

q.q: What are the next steps in the process?
q.a: Two more candidates are being interviewed; everyone will hear by next Wednesday, and the final stage is a short technical test.

gaps.s: Each new engineer has a ___ for the first six months.
The final stage is a short ___ test.

title: The career gap
lines: I notice there's a gap of about eighteen months on your CV. Could you tell me about that?
Of course. After my father became ill, I decided to step away from work to care for him. It was a difficult period, but I don't regret it.
I'm sorry to hear that. How did you keep your skills up to date during that time?
I made a point of it. I completed two online courses in project management, and I did some freelance design work for a local firm.
And how do you feel about returning to a full-time role now?
Honestly, I'm keen to get back. The break gave me perspective, and I think it made me more organised, because I had to juggle a lot of responsibilities.
That's helpful to know. Some people find the first few months back quite demanding.
I'm sure it will take some adjustment, but I've prepared for it, and I'd rather be upfront about the gap than hide it.

q.q: Why does the candidate have a gap on his CV?
q.a: He stepped away from work for about eighteen months to care for his father, who became ill.

q.q: How did he keep his skills up to date?
q.a: He completed two online courses in project management and did freelance design work for a local firm.

q.q: How does he present the break in a positive way?
q.a: He says it gave him perspective and made him more organised, because he had to juggle many responsibilities, and he prefers to be upfront about it.

gaps.s: I decided to step ___ from work to care for him.
I had to ___ a lot of responsibilities.
I'd rather be ___ about the gap than hide it.

title: Turning down an offer
lines: Thanks for calling back. I take it you've reached a decision?
I have, and I wanted to tell you personally rather than by email. I'm afraid I've decided to decline the offer.
I'm sorry to hear that. May I ask what tipped the balance?
Of course. It wasn't the salary, which was more than fair. It's that the other role would let me lead a team from the outset, and at this point in my career that's what I need.
I understand. For what it's worth, we'd have been happy to revisit the scope of the role.
That's kind of you, and I genuinely considered it. But I'd rather not ask you to reshape a position around me, only for it to feel like a compromise on both sides.
That's a very mature way of looking at it. I hope our paths cross again.
So do I. I was very impressed by the team, and I'd be glad to stay in touch.

q.q: Why did the candidate call rather than send an email?
q.a: Because he wanted to tell the interviewer personally that he was declining the offer.

q.q: What made him choose the other job?
q.a: Not the salary, which was fair, but the chance to lead a team from the start, which he needs at this point in his career.

q.q: Why does he not accept the offer to change the role?
q.a: He doesn't want the company to reshape the position around him, because it would feel like a compromise for both sides.

gaps.s: May I ask what tipped the ___?
The other role would let me lead a team from the ___.
Only for it to feel like a ___ on both sides.
